result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.add_full_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add a complete graph (clique) to the current graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L3365-L3447){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.add_full_graph( n, type=None, label=True, rel=None, keep_loops=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Complete graph](/assets/graphs/add-full-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three complete graphs side by side: a triangle for n=3, a square with both diagonals for n=4, and a hexagon with every chord for n=6. Every pair of nodes is joined, giving 3, 6, and 15 edges." width="100%"} Creates `n` nodes where every node is connected to every other node. In a complete graph with `n` nodes, there are `n(n - 1) / 2` edges (without self-loops). ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional node type/category for all nodes. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, label nodes with their IDs. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional relationship label for all edges. [keep_loops]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, include self-loops (adding n more edges). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A complete graph connects every pair of nodes, so `n` nodes produce `n(n-1)/2` edges -- here, `4 * 3 / 2 = 6`: ::: {#43b27e1b .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_full_graph(n=4) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (4, 6) ``` ::: :::
